items.title: Section: The Brief Summary — Four Correct Tasks, and Wakeful Practice Closes

items.zh: 謂常勤修習覺寤瑜伽所有士夫補特伽羅，略有四種正所作事。何等為四？一者、乃至覺寤，常不捨離所修善品，無間常委修善法中，勇猛精進。二者、以時而臥，不以非時。三者、無染污心而習睡眠，非染污心。四者、以時覺寤，起不過時。是名四種常勤修習覺寤瑜伽所有士夫補特伽羅正所作事。依此四種正所作事，諸佛世尊為聲聞眾宣說修習覺寤瑜伽。
items.en: As for any person who constantly and diligently cultivates wakeful practice, there are, in brief, four correct tasks. What are the four? First, up until sleep, one never abandons the wholesome practices one cultivates, applying oneself to them without interruption, earnestly and diligently. Second, one lies down only at the proper time, not at an improper time. Third, one sleeps without a defiled mind, never with a defiled mind. Fourth, one wakes at the proper time, never rising later than one should. These are the four correct tasks of any person who constantly and diligently cultivates wakeful practice. Based on these four correct tasks, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, teach the assembly of hearer-disciples the cultivation of wakeful practice.

items.zh: 云何宣說？謂若說言：於晝日分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心；於初夜分經行宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。由此言故，宣說第一正所作事。謂乃至覺寤，常不捨離所修善品，無間常委修善法中，勇猛精進。若復說言：出住處外洗濯其足，還入住處，右脇而臥，重累其足。由此言故，宣說第二正所作事。謂以時而臥；不以非時。若復說言：住光明想、正念、正知、思惟起想巧便而臥。由此言故，宣說第三正所作事。謂無染污心而習睡眠，非染污心。若復說言：於夜後分速疾覺寤，經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。由此言故，宣說第四正所作事。謂以時覺寤；起不過時。

items.title: Wakeful Practice's Harder Points Clarified, and the Whole Teaching Closes

items.zh: 此中所說住光明想、正念、正知、思惟起想巧便臥者，顯由二緣，無染污心而習睡眠，非染污心。謂由正念，及由正知。復由二緣以時覺寤，起不過時。謂由住光明想，及由思惟起想。此復云何？由正念故，於善所緣攝斂而臥；由正知故，於善所緣若心退失，起諸煩惱，即便速疾能正了知。如是名為由二緣故，無染污心而習睡眠，非染污心。由住光明想，及思惟起想，無重睡眠，非睡眠纏能遠隨逐。如是名為由二緣故，以時覺寤，起不過時。如是宣說常勤修習覺寤瑜伽所有略義，及前所說廣辯釋義，總說名為初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽。
items.en: What is said here — lying down skilfully abiding in the perception of light, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and the intention to rise — reveals that sleeping without a defiled mind depends on two conditions: mindfulness, and clear comprehension. And waking at the proper time, never oversleeping, likewise depends on two conditions: the perception of light, and the intention to rise. …Through mindfulness, one lies down with the mind drawn in towards a wholesome object; through clear comprehension, if the mind should slip from that wholesome object and an affliction arise, one correctly recognises it at once. …Through the perception of light and the intention to rise, sleep is not heavy, and one is not pursued far by the grip of sleep. Thus has been explained the brief summary of constantly and diligently cultivating wakeful practice, which, together with the detailed exposition given before, is together called the constant, diligent cultivation of wakeful practice in the first watch and the last watch of the night.

items.title: Section: Clear Awareness in Conduct Opens — Nine Everyday Contexts

items.zh: 云何名為正知而住？謂如有一，若往、若還正知而住，若覩、若瞻正知而住，若屈、若伸正知而住，持僧伽胝及以衣鉢正知而住，若食、若飲、若噉、若甞正知而住，若行、若住、若坐、若臥正知而住，於覺寤時正知而住，若語、若默正知而住，解勞睡時正知而住。若往、若還正知住者，云何為往？云何為還？云何往還正知而住？
items.en: What is meant by clear awareness in conduct? It is like one who maintains clear awareness whether going or returning; maintains clear awareness whether seeing incidentally or gazing deliberately; maintains clear awareness whether bending or extending the limbs; maintains clear awareness while carrying the great robe, the other robes, and the bowl; maintains clear awareness while eating, drinking, chewing, or tasting; maintains clear awareness whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; maintains clear awareness while awake; maintains clear awareness whether speaking or silent; and maintains clear awareness even while resting from fatigue in sleep.

items.title: Going and Returning: Knowing "I Go, I Return"

items.zh: 所言往者，謂如有一，往詣聚落，往聚落間；往詣家屬，往家屬間；往詣道場，往道場間。所言還者，謂如有一，從聚落還，聚落間還；從家屬還，家屬間還；從道場還，道場間還。所言往還正知住者，謂於自往，正知我往；及於自還，正知我還。
items.en: Going means: it is like one who journeys to a village, or among villages; journeys to a household, or among households; journeys to a monastery, or among monasteries. Returning means: it is like one who returns from a village, or from among villages; returns from a household, or from among households; returns from a monastery, or from among monasteries. Clear awareness in going and returning means: in one's own going, clearly knowing "I go"; and in one's own returning, clearly knowing "I return."

items.title: Section: Which Households to Avoid, and When Not to Visit

items.zh: 於所應往及非所往，能正了知；於所應還及非所還，能正了知。於應往時及非往時，能正了知；於應還時及非還時，能正了知。於其如是如是應往及不應往，能正了知；於其如是如是應還及不應
items.en: One correctly discerns which places should be visited and which should not; one correctly discerns where one should return and where one should not. …There are households one should not visit — which households? Those of criers who announce slaughter, or wine-sellers, or courtesans, or the king, or outcastes, or dog-killers and jailers; or households that persistently slander the Triple Gem without any prospect of change. …One correctly discerns the proper time to go and the improper time. …There are households one may rightly visit, yet one should go neither too early nor too late. If the host's household is occupied with urgent affairs, one should not go; if they are engaged in revelry, or in construction or decoration, in worldly self-indulgence, or in anger and dispute, one should likewise not go.

items.title: Going and Returning Closes: A Fourfold Pattern That Recurs Throughout

items.zh: 彼由成就此正知故，自知而往，自知而還；往所應往，非非所往；還所應還，非非所還；以時往還，不以非時。如其色類動止軌則、禮式、威儀，應往應還，如是而往，如是而還。如是名為若往、若還正知而住。若覩若瞻正知住者，云何為覩？云何為瞻？云何覩瞻正知而住？
items.en: Having accomplished this clear awareness, one knowingly goes and knowingly returns; one goes where one should go, not where one should not, and returns where one should return, not where one should not; one goes and returns at the proper time, not at an improper time; and, in keeping with the deportment, etiquette, and demeanor proper to one's appearance as a monastic, one should go and should return exactly so. This is clear awareness. This is called clear awareness in going and returning.

blocks.text: Wakeful practice is summarised; then clear awareness in conduct begins. Two short passages (0413c04 and elsewhere) are untranslated.

In brief: one practises through the day and first watch; sleeps in the middle watch; "sleeps without a defiled mind"; and "wakes at the proper time". Master Cháng Bǎi: unless ill, a monastic does not sleep by day or with a lamp burning. Venerable Miào Jìng: from passages like this we learn what a monk's daily life was like in the Buddha's time.
Sleeping without defilement depends on mindfulness and clear comprehension; waking on time, on the perception of light and the intention to rise.

Clear awareness covers going and returning, looking and gazing, bending and stretching, carrying robes and bowl, eating and drinking, the four postures and wakefulness, speech and silence, and resting from fatigue.
"One knows: I go; I return." One goes to a village or a household with clear awareness.
Not to the five unsuitable households, and not at the wrong time. Master Cháng Bǎi: the "proclaimers" slaughtered sheep and cried out in the streets beforehand.

Going and returning at the right **time**, with the right **deportment**, to the right **place**, in the right **measure**. Master Cháng Bǎi: time, conduct proper to one's kind, place, and moderation. This pattern recurs in each of the following contexts.

quiz.q: Among the four correct tasks, what are the third and fourth?
options: sleeping without a defiled mind; waking at the proper time, never late
eating and sleeping more; rising late
quiz.why: "Third, one sleeps without a defiled mind, never with a defiled mind. Fourth, one wakes at the proper time, never rising later than one should." Venerable Miào Jìng: a monk who cultivates the path from morning until bedtime is able to attain it.

quiz.q: Citing the Daśabhāṇavāra Vinaya, how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "not at an improper time"?
options: unless ill, one may not sleep in the daytime, nor sleep with a lamp lit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: unless ill, one may not lie down to sleep in the daytime, nor sleep with a lamp burning.

quiz.q: On which two conditions does sleeping without a defiled mind depend?
options: the perception of light and the intention to rise
quiz.why: "Sleeping without a defiled mind depends on two conditions: mindfulness, and clear comprehension." Waking on time depends on the perception of light and the intention to rise. Master Cháng Bǎi: clear comprehension knows whether mindfulness has been lost and returns to it at once.

quiz.q: Reading that the Buddhas teach wakeful practice based on these four tasks, what does Venerable Miào Jìng remark?
options: from this we learn what a monk's day was like in the Buddha's time
no need to practise this today
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: only from this do we learn what a monk's daily life was like in the Buddha's time.

quiz.q: Which contexts does clear awareness in conduct cover, and what are the last two?
options: going and returning, looking, bending, robes and bowl, eating, the four postures, wakefulness, and finally speech and silence, and resting from fatigue
quiz.why: The text runs from going and returning to wakefulness, speech and silence, and resting from fatigue. Master Cháng Bǎi: one keeps clear awareness when speaking and when silent, and even when sleeping to relieve fatigue.

quiz.q: The English has "among villages" and "visit relatives." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read these?
options: 間 is a spot within the village; 家屬 is simply a household, not relatives
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a village is a large area, and 間 is a part within it, a particular spot. 家屬 is simply one household or another.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi layer the closing formula on going and returning?
options: in terms of the matter, the time, and one's role and etiquette
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: going and returning at the proper time concerns time; going and returning in keeping with the deportment proper to one's kind concerns etiquette and role; knowingly going and returning concerns the matter itself.
